one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

words-only.why: Checks 1 and 2 test only what their lines say: padding with fill, a space by default, and returning s unchanged when it is already long enough. Check 4 asks only for exit 0 and fail 0. Check 3 is stricter than its line. The line only says README.md "has a section for every function index.js exports". The FAIL condition, though, needs a heading at level ## or deeper whose text starts with the function name, optionally in backticks (regex `^#{2,}\s+`?name\b`). A real section such as "## Padding strings with padLeft" or "# padLeft" would print MISSING and fail. The words don't require any heading level or wording, so this exact-wording rule should be under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL. The check also says to look at slugify "closely", which is fine, but the heading-format rule alone breaks the criterion.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder's `npm test` maps to the existing script `node --test`. The files it names (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js) are all tracked. The verifier's checks 1 and 2 are `node --input-type=module -e "..."` with single-quoted JS strings inside a double-quoted shell argument. Their imports from './index.js' and 'node:assert/strict' are valid, and `; echo exit=$?` sits outside the quotes. In check 3, bash turns `\\\\` into `\\` and `` \` `` into a backtick. So JS receives `'^#{2,}\\s+`?'` and `'\\b'`, which make the regex `^#{2,}\s+`?name\b`. The `/^#{2,}\s/` literal and `'\n'` pass through unchanged. The `!` inside double quotes only matters in interactive shells with history expansion on, not in scripts. Check 4's `npm test; echo exit=$?` is valid. The repository facts don't show whether package.json has "type": "module", but the ESM commands work either way because `--input-type=module` sets the mode.

catches-traps.why:
I checked the briefs against all three must_catch items, and each one is handled.
1. Builder step 3 says: "also add the missing `## slugify(s)` section". It does this along with the padLeft section in step 2.
2. Verifier Check 3 gets the list of exported functions from index.js and prints it. It prints MISSING for any export that has no README heading. Its PASS line names the four exports: "this includes slugify and padLeft as well as capitalize and truncate". It FAILs on any MISSING name, and it says to look at slugify closely.
3. Verifier Check 1 runs `assert.equal(padLeft('42', 5), '   42');`. That calls padLeft without a fill argument and checks that it pads with spaces.

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked both briefs against the two must_not items.

Item 1: Check 3 cannot pass when slugify has no section. It lists every function export at runtime and checks each against the README headings. If slugify has no heading, the script prints "MISSING: slugify" and the PASS condition fails. The shell escaping turns into a working regex. The brief also adds "slugify had no README section, so look at it closely."

Item 2: none of the PASS conditions goes further than its line. Check 1 asserts only the padding and the default space. Check 2 asserts only that s comes back unchanged. Fill length and parameter count only appear as advisory notes, outside PASS/FAIL. Check 3 accepts a heading at any level from ## down that starts with the function name, with an optional backtick. It does not demand the builder's exact `## name(...)` format. That is a loose reading of "section", though a heading that doesn't start with the name would fail it. Check 4 needs exit 0 and `# fail 0`, which is what node --test normally prints.
